title: Words That Belong Together
text:
Strong collocations give academic writing a natural and precise tone. Writers usually say they 'conduct research' or 'draw a conclusion', because these word pairs are fixed by long use rather than by logic. A learner who chooses a combination at random may produce sentences that are grammatical but sound unfamiliar to native readers.

Collocations are best acquired through extensive reading and careful note-taking. When students record phrases in context, they notice which verbs and nouns regularly appear together. Over time, this awareness helps them write with greater accuracy and confidence.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do writers usually say?
What do students record, according to paragraph two?
Why might an unfamiliar combination sound odd to native readers?
options: Because it breaks a grammar rule
Because it is not the conventional pattern readers expect

questions.text: What can be inferred about the benefit of noticing collocations in context?
options: It removes the need for reading
It helps writers choose combinations more accurately
